what_its_for: Treating and preventing clots in the veins and in the lungs.
pros: Decades of outcome evidence; effect can be measured and adjusted by a blood test.
cons: Needs regular blood tests; many food and medicine interactions; bleeding risk.
common_side_effects: bleeding;bruising;rarely tissue damage from skin blood-vessel clots
cautions: Carries a bleeding warning; not used in pregnancy except for mechanical heart valves.

what_its_for: Lowering the risk of clots and stroke caused by an irregular heartbeat.
pros: Proven to cut stroke risk in atrial fibrillation; dose can be guided by a blood test.
cons: Needs regular monitoring; interacts with many foods and medicines; bleeding risk.
cautions: Carries a bleeding warning; stopping it suddenly raises clot and stroke risk.

what_its_for: Lowering the risk of death and of a further heart attack after one has happened.
pros: Label-supported for reducing repeat heart attack and clot-related events.
cons: Bleeding risk and frequent monitoring make it harder to use than antiplatelet tablets.
cautions: Carries a bleeding warning; never start or stop it without the treating doctor.

what_its_for: Treating and preventing clots in the veins and in the lungs, given by injection.
pros: Works within hours, so it is used when fast anticoagulation is needed.
cons: Injection only, usually in hospital; needs monitoring; bleeding risk.
common_side_effects: bleeding;bruising at the injection site;low platelet count
cautions: Must not be used by anyone who has had heparin-induced low platelets.

what_its_for: Short-term clot prevention in atrial fibrillation, given by injection.
pros: Fast onset, useful as a bridge while a tablet anticoagulant takes effect.
cons: Injection only and short acting; not a long-term option; bleeding risk.
common_side_effects: bleeding;bruising at the injection site;low platelet count
cautions: Must not be used by anyone who has had heparin-induced low platelets.

what_its_for: Making platelets less sticky, to lower the risk of a further heart attack or stroke.
pros: Cheap, widely available, and backed by large outcome trials in established heart disease.
cons: Irritates the stomach and raises bleeding risk; not suitable for everyone.
cautions: Raises bleeding risk, more so with other blood thinners; avoid with active stomach ulcers.
source_note: every US openFDA label for aspirin is an over-the-counter analgesic monograph and does not carry the cardiovascular indication, so this row rests on established pharmacology; the fetched label (set_id 0058175f-3474-40c3-a046-6cfaec86d84b) was read for its warnings only

what_its_for: Making platelets less sticky after a heart attack, a stroke or a stent.
pros: Strong outcome evidence after heart attack and stenting; no routine blood test needed.
cons: Bleeding risk; works poorly in people with certain liver-enzyme gene variants.
cautions: Must not be used during active bleeding; tell any dentist or surgeon before a procedure.

what_its_for: Lowering blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise.
pros: First-choice tablet; long safety record; does not usually cause low sugar on its own.
cons: Stomach upset is common at first; cannot be used with poor kidney function.
common_side_effects: nausea;diarrhoea;metallic taste;low vitamin B12 over time
cautions: Carries a lactic acidosis warning; not used when kidney function is severely reduced.

what_its_for: Prompting the pancreas to release more insulin in type 2 diabetes.
pros: Lowers blood sugar quickly and is inexpensive.
cons: Real risk of low blood sugar, especially if meals are missed; can add weight.
common_side_effects: low blood sugar;weight gain;nausea;rarely a drop in red blood cells
cautions: Not for type 1 diabetes; skipping meals can cause dangerous low blood sugar.

what_its_for: Replacing or supplementing the body's own insulin to control blood sugar.
pros: Works for anyone and can be adjusted precisely; essential when tablets are not enough.
cons: Injections and monitoring are needed; low blood sugar is the main hazard.
common_side_effects: low blood sugar;weight gain;injection-site reactions;low potassium
cautions: Must not be used during a low-sugar episode; never share a pen or needle.
source_note: openFDA SPL label, set_id b60e8dd0-1d48-4dc9-87fd-e14675255e8c effective 20260701 (data/raw/openfda_labels.json)

what_its_for: Making the body's tissues respond better to its own insulin.
pros: Improves insulin sensitivity and keeps working over a long period.
cons: Causes fluid retention and weight gain; can worsen heart failure; raises fracture risk.
cautions: Carries a heart failure warning and must not be started in moderate or severe heart failure.

what_its_for: Strengthening the heart's contraction in mild to moderate heart failure.
pros: Long clinical history; eases symptoms and reduces hospital admissions for heart failure.
cons: The safe and toxic blood levels are very close; needs monitoring.
common_side_effects: nausea;loss of appetite;confusion;visual disturbance;slow or irregular pulse
cautions: Low potassium makes toxicity more likely; many medicines and herbs change its blood level.

what_its_for: Slowing the resting heart rate in long-standing atrial fibrillation.
pros: Effective for resting rate control and usable when blood pressure is low.
cons: Narrow safety margin; does not control the rate during exercise; no stroke protection.
common_side_effects: nausea;loss of appetite;confusion;visual disturbance;slow or irregular pulse
cautions: Does not prevent stroke; low potassium and many interactions raise toxicity risk.

what_its_for: Lowering blood pressure by slowing the heart and reducing its workload.
pros: Lowers blood pressure and the stroke and heart attack risk that comes with it.
cons: Causes tiredness and cold hands; can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar.
cautions: Not for people with a very slow pulse or heart block; never stop it abruptly.

what_its_for: Protecting the heart after a heart attack and easing angina.
pros: Label-supported after heart attack and for angina; well-established.
cons: Tiredness and slow pulse are common; masks low-blood-sugar warning signs.
cautions: Stopping suddenly can trigger chest pain or a heart attack; reduce only with a doctor.

what_its_for: Lowering blood pressure by slowing the heart and reducing its workload.
pros: Lowers blood pressure and the stroke and heart attack risk that comes with it.
cons: Causes tiredness and dizziness; can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar.
cautions: Not for severe slow pulse, heart block or uncontrolled heart failure; never stop abruptly.

what_its_for: Protecting the heart after a heart attack and easing angina.
pros: Label-supported for reducing death after a heart attack.
cons: Tiredness and slow pulse are common; masks low-blood-sugar warning signs.
cautions: Stopping suddenly can worsen angina or trigger a heart attack.

what_its_for: Easing the workload on a weakened heart in stable heart failure.
pros: Improves survival in stable heart failure when built up slowly.
cons: Can worsen symptoms at first; unsuitable while heart failure is uncontrolled.
cautions: Only the slow-release form is used for heart failure, and only once the patient is stable.
source_note: openFDA SPL label, set_id 00940cc5-d2eb-4841-9138-de97d7b1c674 effective 20260727 (data/raw/openfda_labels.json); the heart-failure indication belongs to the extended-release succinate form, not the immediate-release tartrate label fetched here

what_its_for: Relaxing the blood vessels so blood pressure falls.
pros: Once-daily, well tolerated, and works well in Indian and older populations.
cons: Commonly causes ankle swelling; does not slow the heart rate.
cautions: Ankle swelling can be mistaken for heart failure; tell the doctor if it appears.

what_its_for: Blocking a hormone that tightens blood vessels, so blood pressure falls.
pros: Well tolerated, protects the kidneys in diabetes, and rarely causes cough.
cons: Can raise potassium and reduce kidney function; needs blood tests.
cautions: Carries a fetal toxicity warning and must be stopped if pregnancy occurs.
